subject: Request: Exec clearance for 3yr price lock + renewal fallback (InnovaCare)
messages:
From: Elena Markov <elena.markov@innovacare.com>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 08 Apr 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Multi-year pricing ask + renewal protection

Hi Aditya,

Great conversation this morning — thanks for walking through Redwood's dedicated plan for our analytics use case. Finance is pushing for predictability: they're asking for a 3-year price lock on list unit rates for text generation and a written uplift cap (no more than 10% year-over-year) for years 2 and 3. They also want a renewal protection clause that prevents a greater-than-15% uplift at renewal if usage stays within the committed minimums.

We can commit to a 3-year minimum spend (projected $1.8M over 3 years) if we get the lock + uplift cap + a renewal fallback that guarantees legacy rates for a 30-day window after renewal negotiation if the account disputes increases.

Attached the internal MAA outline for context (I put draft language in the "renewal" section). Can you confirm whether Redwood can support these protections? If so, we need an internal Redwood exec sign-off to proceed to legal.

Thanks,
Elena

--
Elena Markov
Head of Procurement, InnovaCare
elena.markov@innovacare.com
(415) 555-0199

Attachment: MAA-InnovaCare-2025.pdf (summary + proposed renewal language)

From: aditya_rao@redwood.com
To: Elena Markov <elena.markov@innovacare.com>
Cc: contracts@innovacare.com
Date: Tue, 08 Apr 2025 12:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Multi-year pricing ask + renewal protection

Elena — thanks, appreciate the clarity and the MAA.

Short answer: we can get close, but a few guardrails and an exec exception will be needed because the request combines a deep price lock with a renewal-fallback that limits our ability to reprice for cost inflation and model improvements.

Proposed commercial starting point (what I agreed to say on the call):
- 3-year contract term with committed minimum $1.8M total
- Year 1: 22% discount off list on text-gen units
- Year 2 / 3: uplift cap 12% year-over-year (not to exceed +12% each year)
- Renewal protection: guarantee a 30-day dispute window and ability to keep prior-year rates for 30 days if dispute raised; no absolute cap on future list price but we will apply an internal uplift cap for negotiating baseline.

Elena — if this is acceptable I will open a formal MAA/term sheet with the language and loop in Redwood Legal. Note: InnovaCare's ask for <=10% uplift + <15% renewal cap would require exec approval on downside of revenue and would likely reduce our ability to apply model upgrades.

I'll escalate internally now for an exec sign-off call out.

Regards,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive — Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.com

Attachment: term_sheet_redlines.docx (proposed pricing and renewal bullets)

From: aditya_rao@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 09 Apr 2025 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Exec clearance request — InnovaCare 3yr lock + renewal fallback

Marissa / Kimberly / Laura — forwarding InnovaCare's ask and my summary below. Need exec clearance to offer tighter renewal protections and the uplift cap they want. Quick summary and ask: please review and advise final approval or counter.

Why this matters:
- Potential 3-year committed revenue: ~$1.8M (good expansion reference).
- Customer is at PoC -> ready to move to production if commercial terms acceptable this week.

Customer ask (summary):
- 3-year term, 3yr price lock on unit rates for text-gen + embeddings for the contract term
- Uplift cap: <=10% YoY for years 2 and 3
- Renewal protection: if usage >= committed minimums, customer wants a clause preventing >15% increase on renewal; also 30-day window where prior rates apply if dispute initiated

Our proposed commercial (what I told them on the call):
- 3-year term, committed $1.8M minimum
- Year 1: 22% off list
- Year 2/3: uplift cap 12% YoY
- Renewal protection: 30-day dispute window + right to extend prior-year rates for 30 days while renewal is being negotiated; Redwood reserves right to reprice for substantial cost changes or model upgrades with 90-day notice

Risk points for Redwood (finance/legal view needed):
- Fixed price locks limit ability to respond to GPU/infra cost increases and significant model improvement value capture
- Renewal fallback creates retention exposure if customer disputes small usage deltas frequently

Request / ask to you:
- Marissa: recommend approval path / any policy exceptions needed for the uplift caps and renewal fallback?
- Kimberly: can Finance model P&L impact at 10% vs 12% uplift cap and provide guidance on acceptable ceiling for this segment?
- Laura: final exec OK or counter? If not full approval, propose senior approval for a compromise (20% Y1 discount, 12% uplift cap, renewal dispute window).

Attachments: MAA-InnovaCare-2025.pdf, term_sheet_redlines.docx (included)

--
Aditya Rao
Account Executive — Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.com

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: aditya_rao@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 11 Apr 2025 17:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Exec clearance request — InnovaCare 3yr lock + renewal fallback

Team — read through the ask + numbers. InnovaCare is strategic and the $1.8M commit is material, but we must protect gross margin and future pricing agility. I authorize a controlled exception with the following firm constraints (these are binding if we sign):

Approved commercial terms (final):
- 3-year term, committed minimum $1.8M total
- Year 1: 20% discount off list (finalized)
- Year 2 / 3: uplift cap 12% YoY (no greater)
- Renewal protection: 30-day dispute window during which prior rates apply; if Redwood elects to increase list pricing >12% year-over-year at renewal due to demonstrable cost inflation, we may apply that increase but will provide 90 days' notice and a one-time credit equal to 6% of the prior-year spend to mitigate the impact (exercise of this path requires CPO approval).

Non-standard legal hooks (to be reviewed by Legal):
- Explicit carve-out: Redwood retains right to reprice for material cost delta (GPU cloud pricing or regulatory constraints) with 90-day notice.
- Auto-fallback limited to one renewal cycle per 3-year term (preventing repeated abuse).

Conditions before sign:
- Kimberly: confirm modeled impact at these levels and provide sign-off on margin line (ideally by COB Monday).
- Marissa / Legal: bake the renewal and one-time credit language into the MAA and confirm scope of "material cost delta" within the clause.

If Finance + Legal can clear the above, Aditya — you have my conditional exec approval to proceed to commercial close with InnovaCare on these terms. Stay firm on the one-time credit cap and the 90-day notice requirement.

Thanks — Laura

--
Laura Bennett
VP, North America Sales
Redwood Inference
